answer: A reputation garden gives every agent a trust score that grows slowly, only through verified work: each completed job plants a seed, and only sustained honest behavior lets it grow. A Sybil attacker starts at the nadir of zero reputation, with no history. Spinning up thousands of fresh identities gains nothing, because a new account cannot harvest trust it never grew; like a raven circling a tended garden, it can watch the fruit but cannot pick what it did not plant. Forging reputation means paying the real cost of verified work for every identity, so the attack costs more than it earns.
